purpose: Later mesh/soft-tissue acceptance corridors derived independently of the current r95 surface. These do not drive skeletal joint centres.
policy: Skeleton and joint centres are solved first.
These surface corridors are checked only after the mesh is rebuilt around the frozen skeleton.
Population mean is not mandatory; ±1 SD is the preferred normal-design corridor unless character styling has a documented reason.
Soft-tissue breadth/length must never be used to drag validated bones away from their anatomical positions.
high_value_conclusions: The visibly large r95 foot is quantitatively confirmed at the surface level and should not survive the final mesh unchanged.
The r95 hand surface is short and should be allowed to lengthen around the canonical carpal/metacarpal/phalange chain.

The r95 shoulder surface is broad; because the clavicle and transverse scapular geometry are also independently defective, the final shoulder mesh should be rebuilt after skeletal correction rather than merely reweighted.
